Today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate version contains a short video that appears to showcase the Visual Intelligence feature on Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods. Check it out below.

macOS 26.7 contains a demonstration video of camera-equipped AirPods

MacRumors discovered a short video included in today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate version, in which a man wearing AirPods appears to ask Siri to record the book he is reading, and Siri's voiceover says:

In the video, the camera itself is not visible, and the earbuds look very similar to the current AirPods Pro. The most obvious difference is the stem, which appears slightly thicker.

Aaron Perris also posted the same video on X:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that Apple may launch camera-equipped AirPods this year, with the codename B790. Earlier, MacRumors also found B790-related information in the macOS 26.7 candidate version, including code for an 'image stream'.

Interestingly, these AirPods are reportedly separate from another camera-equipped model that Bloomberg said Apple has been developing under the codename B798, which is expected to launch in 2027.

Based on Apple's decision to include this demonstration in the macOS 26.7 candidate version, these camera-equipped AirPods are very likely to make their official debut at next month's iPhone launch event.

What are your thoughts on this video? Feel free to share them in the comments section.
